source_review.notes: Checked all thirteen references. Current StatefulSet, PersistentVolume, StorageClass, VolumeSnapshot, force-delete, disruption, operator, node-shutdown, CSI snapshot, and etcd recovery claims were verified against primary project documentation; quorum reasoning was checked against the Raft paper, contingency concepts against NIST SP 800-34r1, and platform framing against the CNCF white paper. Kubernetes mechanics are consistently separated from database/protocol guarantees.

evidence: Reviewed service contract S=(A,C,M,R,F,V,T,U,B,O,L), quorum q and failure f, failure-domain sets, RPO/RTO time variables, and incarnation I=(m,g,e).
Confirmed symbols are defined before use and all floor, ellipsis, and set notation uses GitHub-renderable dollar delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates protocol, topology, recovery, and incarnation identity without implying Kubernetes objects establish the mathematical premises.

evidence: Recomputed q=floor(n/2)+1 and f=n-q for n=3..7: (2,1), (3,1), (3,2), (4,2), and (4,3).
Checked the three-zone placements in Answer 2 against each majority threshold, including the 4-voter 2/1/1 counterexample.
Executed the ten-profile inventory and reproduced every expected aggregate.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Every explicit quorum and inventory value recomputes; the chapter does not infer fault-domain independence from the arithmetic.

evidence: Verified f=n-(floor(n/2)+1)=floor((n-1)/2) for integer n.
Verified any two subsets larger than n/2 must intersect by contradiction from disjoint cardinality exceeding n.
Checked achieved RPO window t_i-t_r and recovery time t_o-t_0 have time units and explicitly defined origins.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Symbolic results are correct within the stated simple majority model; application correctness, durability, timing, membership, and failure independence remain separate premises.

evidence: Reviewed one-zone placement, even voter count, simultaneous maintenance and failure, unknown-node force deletion, stale writer, wrong data generation, and ReadWriteOnce same-node concurrency.
Reviewed disk full, corrupt replica, incompatible binary/data rollback, missing historical key, corrupt/latest backup, realistic large restore, control-plane outage, and multi-region split brain.
Reviewed empty bootstrap, member add/remove interruption, retained PVC/snapshot/backup, dead operator finalizer, legal hold, and deletion/erasure boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary coverage targets correlated failures and cross-layer ambiguity rather than only happy-path StatefulSet provisioning.

evidence: Traced authority-first admission, controller/protocol separation, fenced incarnation, membership distinction, topology independence, storage fit, restore testing, role-aware health, compatibility, operator governance, and retirement through all sections.
Verified each StatefulSet, PVC/access-mode, snapshot, PDB, force-delete, node-shutdown, and operator mechanism has an explicit non-guarantee.
Checked worked examples and answers preserve the same lifecycle and recovery boundaries.
invariant_checking.notes: No claim treats stable ordinal, bound storage, ready Pod, PDB, replica, snapshot, backup job, managed provider, or resource deletion as stronger correctness evidence.

evidence: Reviewed majority quorum intersection: two quorums each larger than n/2 cannot be disjoint.
Reviewed the chapter's explicit limitation that intersection alone does not prove correctness, durability, freshness, membership agreement, or failure independence.
Checked the incarnation/fencing argument requires authoritative enforcement of current epoch, not only lease acquisition.
proof_review.notes: The bounded mathematical claim is valid; application and infrastructure conclusions are conditional on separately named mechanisms and evidence.

evidence: The quorum argument is labeled as a set-intersection result and explicitly not a Kubernetes availability guarantee.
RPO/RTO are expressed as achieved measures with declared origins rather than presumed from schedule or startup settings.
Managed-service, operator, backup, and recovery claims consistently require validation rather than asserting inherent correctness.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Mathematical reasoning, engineering assurance, provider behavior, and empirical recovery evidence are appropriately distinguished.

evidence: The executable inventory is explicitly labeled synthetic review evidence and names all outcomes it cannot prove.
The chapter requires realistic isolated restores and fault injection instead of claiming scheduled backups or small fixtures prove production recovery.
Current provider behaviors are attributed to versioned/retrieved documentation and not presented as measured service performance.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic, mathematical, documentation-derived, and required production/recovery evidence remain separate; no external review is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the full model from authoritative state and admission through identity, membership, quorum, fencing, storage, health, maintenance, scale, upgrade, operator governance, security, restore, DR, migration, and retirement. The chapter consistently distinguishes replicas, snapshots, backups, and recovery, and treats state correctness as a cross-layer contract.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementability for managed-service bindings, domain operators, constrained StatefulSets, headless discovery, per-member claims, topology-aware storage, ReadWriteOnce/ReadWriteOncePod semantics, membership procedures, fencing, PDB-aware maintenance, compatible rollout, application-consistent backup, isolated restore, failover/failback, and residual-data deletion. Runbooks include explicit stop conditions and evidence.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified required section order, dense review sheet, first-principles exposition, defined notation, conditional proof structure, twelve trade-offs, twenty misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, cross-program connections, thirteen references, and five progressive exercises with complete model answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
